text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday, prepared for Reuters by the Estonian news agency, ETA. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Priit Saksing, former director general of the rare metals plant Silmet is suspected of embezzlement.
- A junior politician is suspected of having bought the votes of students in order to win elections to the Tartu University students' council.
- A draft law on the institution of a state ombudsman is being prepared; the official would help citizens protest against the government.
- The Baltic Assembly called for the abolition of capital punishment.
- Human rights experts have recommended Estonia amend its policy towards aliens, including the law on citizenship.
- The Baltic prime ministers agreed in Parnu on April 26 to establish free trade between the three Baltic countries.
- Europe's big nations do not support the admission of the Baltic states to NATO, WEU Assembly defence committee chairman Guenther Martens told the Baltic Assembly on Sunday.
- Estonia will reduce the number of its consular officials in Finland and Sweden due to visa-free travel.
- The Estonian delegation left for Dublin on Sunday to attend the Eurovision song contest.
- The decision by Tallinn city decision to sell its shares in Tallinna Pank means the emergence of a new strategic investor, probably from outside Estonia.
- Trilateral negotiations between the government, trade unions and employers ended with an agreement to allocate support for the staff of bankrupt companies.
- A third mobile telephone network Q GSM has begun to operate. Prices are described as good but the range is still limited to Tallinn, Tartu, Parnu and Narva.
